### Goal
Complete migration steps 3–8, ensure request-ID binding in HTTP handlers, then address the nightly reconciliation refund double-counting bug.

### Constraints and rules
Use `db-stg-2.internal`; ignore stale `config/staging.yaml`. Never expose fields ending `_secret`, `_token`, or `_fingerprint`; use `ledgerly.sanitizers.safe_customer_context`. Keep commits small. Do not retry the six-hour Celery visibility timeout.

### Key decisions and facts
Tenacity refactor is deferred to next sprint. Logging includes safe `request_id`; missing request IDs format as null. SQLAlchemy uses `DeclarativeBase`, UTC-aware timestamps, and non-legacy invoice pagination. Ruff passes. Avatar migration found 18,432 files, wrote checksums, recorded a migration run, and synced PNG/JPG files to S3.

### Ruled out
No PDF, billing, or repository regressions. Scheduler DST bug was fixed by constructing local recurrence directly and converting to UTC.

### Progress
Logging and health tests pass. Billing tests: 18 passed, 1 skipped. Full suite previously: 142 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed, then health test was fixed. Scheduler tests now pass, including a new midnight-DST regression test.

### Next steps
Run the new midnight test and full suite; verify/patch request-ID binding in every HTTP handler. Continue migration steps 5–8 in order. Investigate `ledgerly/jobs/reconcile.py` refund double-counting, with focused regression tests.

Paste exact test output, not paraphrases. Treat fields ending `_secret`, `_token`, or `_fingerprint` as restricted; copy only via `ledgerly.sanitizers.safe_customer_context`.

Finish scoped-session lifecycle review, rerun full tests, then implement `tenacity`. Afterwards execute all eight avatar migration steps sequentially. Visually compare three generated PDFs when practical.
